item.title: Four new mayors on rolling a grenade down the road for future generations
item.description: These mayors just won office for the first time. They’re already worried they’re going to end up lumping their children and grandchildren with a huge bill for broken infrastructure. A record-breaking crop of first-time mayors won office at October’s local body elections. Thirty-two of New Zealand’s 78 councils are now led by people who’ve never been in the top job before. item.description: How a Trumpian beef about interest rates spilled over to New Zealand. When the ancient Roman Republic was facing a crisis such as a war or internal rebellion, the senate could temporarily appoint a single leader with near-absolute power. Their title was dictator.
